transcript.text: You led the migration of a settlement service from a monolith to three services, reducing on-call pages from 30 to 8 per month. Can you walk me through the key challenges you faced during this migration?

I've spent six years as a software engineer, the last three at a payments company in Bengaluru. My biggest piece of work was splitting our settlement service out of the monolith into three services. I wrote the design document, got sign-off from two other teams and ran the cut-over over four weekends. On-call pages dropped from roughly 30 a month to 8. I'm applying now because the decisions I find most interesting, such as what to build and for which merchants, are made one level above me, and I want the business training to make them well.
How did you coordinate with your team and stakeholders to ensure the migration met the desired reliability and performance goals?
transcript.anchor_quote: I wrote the design document, got sign-off from two other teams and ran the cut-over over four weekends

transcript.text: I can't share the transaction volumes or revenue numbers; they're confidential to the company. What I can say is that settlement runs every night for all of our merchants, so an outage there is visible to customers the next morning.
Could you explain the monitoring and rollback mechanisms you put in place during the four-weekend cut-over period to handle any unexpected issues without impacting customers?
transcript.anchor_quote: I wrote the design document, got sign-off from two other teams and ran the cut-over over four weekends

transcript.text: Actually, I managed the whole team for that migration. Well, not formally. There were three of us and I was the one who wrote the plan, but I didn't have anyone reporting to me.
You mentioned you managed the whole team for the migration informally. How did you handle any disagreements or differing opinions within the team during this project?

feedback.summary: The candidate demonstrated clear personal ownership and a good understanding of the scope of a complex technical migration project, communicating key steps and outcomes effectively. They showed motivation linked to wanting a broader impact on business decisions. However, the answers lacked detail on stakeholder coordination, specific monitoring or rollback strategies, and conflict resolution within the team. The candidate shifted off-topic once and chose to stop the session before covering contributions to peers or learning from setbacks.
